notes: C6 has no qualifying primary because the command marker is tested inline at line 289 and the FIFO data paths only relay the transaction under the primary-labeling bars.
The diagram and closed set treat the FIFO instances as black boxes; FIFO storage and returned data are therefore reasoned using the specified black-box assumption.

points.reason: A bus write directly overwrites ctrl.enable, allowing an attacker to disable SPI operation and its dependent functions.
This logic only forwards the enable state into the receive FIFO clear input; it provides no independent unauthorized observation or influence.
This logic only forwards the enable state into the transmit FIFO clear input; it provides no independent unauthorized observation or influence.
The clock generator consumes ctrl.enable as an operational control, but does not store or independently modify the enable state.
The interrupt expression uses ctrl.enable as a gating operand but does not expose or independently change the enable state.
The transceiver uses ctrl.enable to enter or leave its operation state, but the enable state is not independently observable or writable there.
This output forwards the stored enable state and does not itself provide an additional modification or observation mechanism.
A bus write overwrites the prescaler, divider, and high-speed settings, allowing timing to be changed or transfers to be slowed.
This block applies the rate settings to generate timing but does not independently expose or modify the stored settings.
The transceiver uses spi_clk_en to pace transfers, but does not store or independently alter the rate configuration.
The bus data is copied into the transmit FIFO input, so changing the bus write changes the payload selected for transmission.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the written transmit word is stored and later returned through rdata_o; the write-data and write-enable port-map lines show the integrity mechanism.
The FIFO word is loaded into rtx_engine.sreg and shifted there, so the transceiver is where the payload can be altered before serial output.
spi_dat_o directly exposes the most significant bit of the transmit shift register.
The external spi_dat_i value is sampled into the receive path, so an altered input changes the received payload.
The receive shift-register value is copied into the receive FIFO write-data path.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the received word enters the FIFO through wdata_i and is later returned through rdata_o for bus response.
A bus read copies rx_fifo.rdata into bus_rsp_o.data, exposing the received payload to the bus.
The bus-written command word, including its chip-select encoding, enters the transmit FIFO input.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the queued command word is stored and returned to the transceiver, so changing the write path can alter or suppress chip-select commands.
The transceiver tests the queued marker and loads rtx_engine.cs_ctrl from the command word, allowing selection state to be changed or omitted.
The bus response only reports cs_ctrl and does not independently modify or block the chip-select state.
This process applies the already stored chip-select state to the output and does not independently change that state.
The bus-written transmit word, including its marker bit, enters the FIFO data path and can be changed before interpretation.
By the black-box FIFO rule, the queued word is stored and returned to the transceiver, so its marker can be altered or prevented from reaching the decoder.
The inline test of tx_fifo.rdata(8) selects between chip-select handling and payload serialization, so changing the marker changes the operation.
The process combines enable settings and FIFO or engine status into irq_o, so altered inputs can suppress required interrupts or create spurious ones.
